paras: The Third Street police shooting was an incident in Richmond, Virginia, in August 1910 in which a police officer fired at a Black man he had followed into the yards between Broad and Grace streets. The man was not hurt, and the officer, after checking his explanation, found that he had told the truth. The Richmond Planet reported it under the headline "A Colored Man Has Narrow Escape."

The man, who lived on West Leigh Street, had served on a committee running an excursion to West Point, and the return train was late getting into Richmond. According to the Planet, he went into a lot off Third Street to see his sister.

On what the Planet called "last Tuesday night," a police officer saw the man go into an alley between Broad and Grace streets and followed him, but lost him among the yards. The officer searched the neighborhood without finding him and waited. When he heard a gate slam and saw the man, he called on him to halt and then fired at him. Coming up, the officer found the man standing with both hands raised above his head.
The officer "carried him back," checked his account, and found it true. No arrest, charge or inquiry into the shooting appears in the coverage, and neither the man nor the officer is named.

The only report found is a short front-page paragraph in the Richmond Planet, a Black weekly, on August 20, 1910. The Planet offered no editorial comment, but its headline and its line "He was a colored man" put the man's race at the center of the item. The paragraph ran in a column of Richmond items that went on to note a fight on the West Point excursion train and to reprint, almost word for word, the Times-Dispatch's August 12 account of a white Henrico County man arrested for holding up a car with a Black chauffeur at pistol point. No white-press version of the shooting itself was found.

The date is uncertain: counted from the Planet's issue of Saturday, August 20, "last Tuesday" was August 16, but if the item was taken from a Richmond daily of about August 11 or 12, as the story beside it was, the shooting took place on August 9.

reader.title: Third Street police shooting, Richmond (1910)
bases: A single police officer fired at a Black man he had pursued into a yard; no crowd was involved and the man was unhurt (A2).
The only report is the Richmond Planet's paragraph (A2); no white-press version of the shooting was found, though the Planet's neighboring item was a reprint from the Times-Dispatch (A1).

accounts.label: Richmond Planet (Black weekly)
accounts.gist: The officer saw the man enter an alley, lost him, heard a gate slam, called halt and fired; the man stood with hands raised, explained the late excursion train and his sister, and the officer found the story true.

framing.detail: Headline 'A Colored Man Has Narrow Escape'; a plain news paragraph with no editorial comment, run in a column of Richmond items including a reprinted white-press arrest story.

versions.value: 1910-08-16 ('last Tuesday night' counted from the Planet's Aug. 20 issue)
1910-08-09 (if the item, like the Tignor story beside it, came from a Richmond daily of about Aug. 11-12)

conflicts.note: The shooting story itself was not found in any daily, so its source and date cannot be confirmed.

sources.note: 'A Colored Man Has Narrow Escape': officer fired at a Black man in a yard off Third Street 'last Tuesday night'; man unhurt, gave an account the officer found true. Same item continues into the unrelated Tignor hold-up story.
quotes: After waiting for some time he heard a gate slam and he saw the man. He called upon him to halt. He then fired at him.
When he came out he saw the man standing and both of his hands raised above his head.
The officer carried him back and found that he told the truth.

set_aside: 'Holds Up Auto at Pistol Point': J. E. Tignor's arrest; the Richmond Planet reprinted this item nearly word for word in the same column as the shooting story, showing that column drew on Richmond daily items of about Aug. 11-12.
Continuation of the Tignor hold-up story (horse test, county jail); not about the shooting. Seen as a search excerpt only.
